profile.research_note: [batch narration moved out of reading 2026-09-02] This CyrusOne campus sits in Loudoun County, Virginia, in and around Sterling, part of the Northern Virginia Ashburn area data center corridor. Wikipedia coverage of CyrusOne states the company purchased 40 acres in Loudoun County in June 2016 for data center construction. CyrusOne was founded in July 2000 by David Ferdman and Larry Bursten, went public in 2013, and was taken private in 2022 when Kohlberg Kravis Roberts and Global Infrastructure Partners acquired it for 15 billion dollars. No building specific address or individual MW figures were located in available sourcing this session.

reading.body:
The Sterling campus spans three buildings, NVA1 through NVA3, totaling 420,000 square feet of technical space and 44 MW of published IT capacity. At 10 kW per rack, a common colocation density, 44 MW supports roughly 4,400 racks; at 40 kW per rack, a common AI training density, the same 44 MW supports roughly 1,100 racks. CyrusOne has not published a per-rack power envelope for this campus, so neither figure is an operator claim. What the capacity does establish is a large, multi-building footprint in Northern Virginia, one of the densest data center markets in the world by any published measure.

The certification stack qualifies the campus to host a wide range of regulated workloads. SOC 1 Type 2 and SOC 2 Type 2 address financial and operational controls for audit purposes. PCI DSS qualifies it for payment card data. HIPAA qualifies it for protected health information. ISO 27001 is an internationally recognized information security management standard. FISMA qualification means the facility can support federal government data handling requirements. TIA-942 is a data center infrastructure standard covering design and construction. No tenants are published.

Among the five Virginia facilities this site has read published megawatt figures for, this campus ranks second at 44 MW out of 233 MW total, giving it roughly 19 percent of the published capacity in the state. Virginia has 326 mapped facilities in total, meaning the vast majority publish no capacity figure, and the 233 MW total is a floor, not a ceiling, on what the state actually hosts. For an AI workload that needs regulated-environment compliance, federal eligibility, and proven scale in an established market, this campus clears the threshold on all three counts.
